# The tools an agent gets

`tonestack mcp start` serves tonestack over the Model Context Protocol: the
catalog, the corpus, building a preset and the pedal itself, as tools with typed
results instead of text to parse.

This page is generated by listing the tools the way a connecting agent lists
them, so it cannot name a tool that is not offered, miss an argument one takes,
or disagree with the description the model is shown.

For adding the server to an agent, see
[workflows/use-it-from-an-agent.md](workflows/use-it-from-an-agent.md). For the
same operations as a person runs them, see [commands.md](commands.md).

## The 15 tools

Alphabetical, which is the order the server lists them in. **writes** is what a
call can change, and **pedal** whether it needs the hardware attached.

| tool | writes | pedal | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`catalog_block`](#catalog_block) | no | no | One block's parameters, their ranges and defaults, and its DSP cost |
| [`catalog_search`](#catalog_search) | no | no | Find blocks the device models, by name, real-world gear, category or instrument |
| [`corpus_model`](#corpus_model) | no | no | How players set one model across measured presets: median and quartiles per parameter |
| [`devices_list`](#devices_list) | no | yes | The Line 6 Helix hardware attached over USB |
| [`preset_build`](#preset_build) | a file | no | Build a .hlx from a shipped rig or a rig file |
| [`preset_export`](#preset_export) | a file | yes | Write one slot to a file: a rig by default, or the device's own .hlx with as=hlx |
| [`preset_import`](#preset_import) | the pedal | yes | Put a .hlx into a slot on the pedal |
| [`preset_select`](#preset_select) | nothing stored | yes | Load a slot on the pedal, as pressing its footswitch does |
| [`preset_show`](#preset_show) | no | yes | One slot on the pedal, read back as a rig |
| [`presets_copy`](#presets_copy) | the pedal | yes | Copy one slot onto another |
| [`presets_list`](#presets_list) | no | yes | Every slot on the attached pedal and what it holds |
| [`presets_swap`](#presets_swap) | the pedal | yes | Exchange two slots |
| [`rig_show`](#rig_show) | no | no | One shipped rig, and the rigs that extend it |
| [`rigs_list`](#rigs_list) | no | no | The rigs that ship with tonestack |
| [`tone_build`](#tone_build) | no | no | Turn a ToneSpec and a Setup into the rig they describe |

## Writing is decided when the server starts

A pedal has no undo and neither has a file, so whoever starts the server
decides, not the agent talking to it. Without `--allow-writes` these tools are
not registered at all: an agent cannot call one, because it cannot see one.

| only with `--allow-writes` | what a call replaces |
| --- | --- |
| `preset_import` | Put a .hlx into a slot on the pedal |
| `presets_copy` | Copy one slot onto another |
| `presets_swap` | Exchange two slots |

Each of those saves what it is about to replace to a file first, the same way
`presets import` does from the command line.

The flag decides one more thing for the tools it does not withhold. These write
a file rather than a slot, so they are offered either way. Without the flag they
refuse a path that already holds a file instead of writing over it.

| offered either way | writes |
| --- | --- |
| `preset_build` | Build a .hlx from a shipped rig or a rig file |
| `preset_export` | Write one slot to a file: a rig by default, or the device's own .hlx with as=hlx |

Everything else is read-only, apart from `preset_select`, which loads a slot the
way pressing its footswitch does and stores nothing.

## Before any tool that reaches the pedal

Quit HX Edit. It claims the editor interface and tonestack cannot have it at the
same time. The tools hold the pedal between calls and let it go once they have
been idle, so the front panel works again without stopping the server.

A tool the table marks **no** under pedal answers from what ships: the catalog,
the corpus, the measured readings and the rigs in the tree. Those need nothing
attached.

## Every tool

### catalog_block

One block's parameters, their ranges and defaults, and its DSP cost.

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | the identifier, such as HD2_AmpSVBeastBrt for a model or mike-dirnt for a rig |

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `based_on` | string | no |
| `cablink` | string | no |
| `category` | string | yes |
| `dsp` | object | yes |
| `id` | string | yes |
| `name` | string | yes |
| `params` | object | yes |
| `prov` | string | yes |
| `stereo` | boolean | yes |
| `subcategory` | string | no |

### catalog_search

Find blocks the device models, by name, real-world gear, category or instrument.
Use this before naming any model: a model it does not find does not exist.

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | string | no | only blocks of one kind, such as amp, cab, drive, dynamics, eq, delay, reverb or modulation |
| `search` | string | no | text in the block's name or in the real-world gear it models |
| `subcategory` | string | no | Line 6's own grouping, such as Guitar or Bass |

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Device` | string | yes |
| `Matched` | array of object | yes |
| `Source` | string | yes |
| `Total` | integer | yes |

### corpus_model

How players set one model across measured presets: median and quartiles per
parameter. A narrow spread is consensus; a wide one is taste.

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | the identifier, such as HD2_AmpSVBeastBrt for a model or mike-dirnt for a rig |

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `block` | object | yes |
| `params` | object | yes |
| `uses` | integer | yes |

### devices_list

The Line 6 Helix hardware attached over USB. HX Edit must be quit for any tool
that reaches the pedal.

Takes no arguments.

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Devices` | array of object | yes |

### preset_build

Build a .hlx from a shipped rig or a rig file. Read what it added and what each
character word moved before putting it on a pedal. Refuses a file already at out
unless the server was started with --allow-writes.

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `out` | string | yes | where to write the .hlx |
| `recipe_id` | string | no | a rig that ships, by identifier; see rigs_list |
| `rig_path` | string | no | a rig file on disk |

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from_recipe` | object | no |
| `from_rig` | object | no |

### preset_export

Write one slot to a file: a rig by default, or the device's own .hlx with
as=hlx. Refuses a file already at out unless the server was started with
--allow-writes.

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | string | no | empty for a rig, which reads on other hardware; hlx for the device's own file |
| `out` | string | yes | where to write the file |
| `slot` | string | yes | a slot as the pedal labels it, 01A to 42C |

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Name` | string | yes |
| `Path` | string | yes |
| `Slot` | integer | yes |

### preset_import

Put a .hlx into a slot on the pedal. Whatever the slot held is saved to a file
first and then gone from the pedal.

Offered only when the server was started with `--allow-writes`.

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | string | yes | the .hlx file to place |
| `slot` | string | yes | a slot as the pedal labels it, 01A to 42C |

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Action` | string | yes |
| `From` | object | yes |
| `Kept` | array of string | yes |
| `Mismatch` | boolean | yes |
| `Path` | string | yes |
| `Replaced` | string | yes |
| `To` | object | yes |

One slot on the pedal, read back as a rig.

### presets_copy

Copy one slot onto another. The destination's old preset is saved to a file

Offered only when the server was started with `--allow-writes`.

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | yes | the source slot, 01A to 42C |
| `to` | string | yes | the destination slot, 01A to 42C |

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Action` | string | yes |
| `From` | object | yes |
| `Kept` | array of string | yes |
| `Mismatch` | boolean | yes |
| `Path` | string | yes |
| `Replaced` | string | yes |
| `To` | object | yes |

### presets_list

Every slot on the attached pedal and what it holds.

Takes no arguments.

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Name` | string | yes |
| `Slots` | array of object | yes |

### presets_swap

Exchange two slots. Both are saved to files first. One slot holding no preset
makes it a move: the preset lands there and the slot it came from is emptied.
Two slots holding no preset are refused.

Offered only when the server was started with `--allow-writes`.

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | yes | the source slot, 01A to 42C |
| `to` | string | yes | the destination slot, 01A to 42C |

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Action` | string | yes |
| `From` | object | yes |
| `Kept` | array of string | yes |
| `Mismatch` | boolean | yes |
| `Path` | string | yes |
| `Replaced` | string | yes |
| `To` | object | yes |

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Answers with:

### rigs_list

The rigs that ship with tonestack.

Takes no arguments.

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dir` | string | yes |
| `Rigs` | array of object | yes |

### tone_build

Turn a ToneSpec and a Setup into the rig they describe. Gear named by hand
resolves against the catalog; gear left unnamed is chosen by measuring a
recording against every block. Read the notes: they say what it could not honour
and what it assumed. Answers with the rig rather than writing a file.

| argument | type | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `setup` | string | no | a Setup file: what they own. Optional; the answer says what it assumed without one |
| `spec` | string | yes | a ToneSpec file: what somebody wants to sound like |

Answers with:

| field | type | always |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notes` | array of object | yes |
| `rig` | object | yes |

## What a call comes back as

Every tool answers with a structured result and one line of text beside it, for
an agent that reads text rather than structure. The structured half is what to
read.

The tables above give the top level of each answer and no further. The full
schema travels with the tool, so an agent already has it, and it is inferred
from the Go type the tool returns rather than written down twice. A `rig` field
is a whole RigSpec: [rigspec.md](rigspec.md) says what is in one.

A field marked **always** is in the schema's `required` list, so an answer
carries it. Anything else can be absent, and absent is not the same as zero. A
tool with nothing to say about a field leaves it out.
